sample_unit: deidentified pediatric pelvic radiographs (with 9 caregiver prompts each; ~95 responses per model)

links.outcome: Radiographic interpretation accuracy and management recommendation specificity of MLLMs for CP hip displacement
links.effect: Diagnostic hallucinations observed (Claude misidentified non-operative cases as bilateral hip replacements); recommendations were generic and failed to measure or apply migration percentage thresholds.
links.quote: While management recommendations were clinically relevant, they remained generic rather than patient-specific, failing to measure or apply migration percentage thresholds.

links.outcome: Whether MLLM diagnostic accuracy supports use as stand-alone diagnostic tool
links.effect: Significant radiographic hallucinations and lack of specific evidence-based guidance preclude standalone diagnostic use; MLLMs suggested as educational adjuncts requiring expert oversight.
links.quote: However, significant radiographic hallucinations and a lack of specific, evidence-based guidance preclude their use as standalone diagnostic tools.

unlisted_practices: Medical disclaimer inclusion rates in MLLM responses to caregiver queries
Directing users to consult an orthopaedic surgeon

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5 Pro) on pediatric radiographs and simulated caregiver prompts for diagnostic accuracy and disclaimer rates, without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
